    arrange(desc(n_entries), theme)

  theme_panel_order <- theme_panel_counts$theme
  theme_panel_labels <- setNames(
    paste0(
      theme_panel_counts$theme,
      " (N = ",
      theme_panel_counts$n_entries,
      ")"
    ),
    theme_panel_counts$theme
  )

  plot_data <- plot_data |>
    group_by(theme, visualization) |>
    mutate(
      n_group = n(),
      point_alpha = if_else(
        fade_sparse & n_group <= a305_sparse_max_n, 0.25, 0.8
      )
    ) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(theme = factor(theme, levels = theme_panel_order))

  boxplot_data <- if (fade_sparse) {
    filter(plot_data, n_group > a305_sparse_max_n)
  } else {
    plot_data
  }

  x_axis_text <- if (angle_x_labels) {
    ggtext::element_markdown(
      size = 20,
      angle = 30,
      hjust = 1,
      vjust = 1,
      lineheight = 0.9,
      margin = margin(t = 8)
    )
  } else {
    ggtext::element_markdown(
      size = 24,
      lineheight = 0.85,
      margin = margin(t = 6)
    )
  }

  ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(
      x = visualization,
      y = median_intensity,
      colour = visualization == "Basic",
      fill = visualization == "Basic"
    )
  ) +
    geom_boxplot(
      data = boxplot_data,
      width = 0.62,
      outlier.shape = NA,
      linewidth = 0.6
    ) +
    ggbeeswarm::geom_beeswarm(
      aes(alpha = point_alpha),
      size = 2.4,
      cex = 1.15,
      priority = "ascending",
      corral = "gutter",
      corral.width = 0.5
    ) +
    facet_wrap(
      vars(theme),
      scales = "free_x",
      ncol = 2,
      labeller = as_labeller(theme_panel_labels)
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = visualization_axis_labels, drop = TRUE) +
    scale_colour_manual(
      values = c(`FALSE` = "#333333", `TRUE` = "#377EB8"),
      guide = "none"
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(`FALSE` = "#D9D9D9", `TRUE` = "#B9D8F2"),
      guide = "none"
    ) +
    scale_alpha_identity() +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(-2.15, 2.15),
      breaks = -2:2,
      labels = intensity_axis_labels,
      minor_breaks = NULL
    ) +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = "Participant-level median evaluation intensity",
      caption = paste(
        "Points represent participants, not individual meaning units.",
        "Panel N is the number of plotted participant-visualization entries.",
        if (fade_sparse) {
          paste0(
            "Faded points without a box: cells with ",
            a305_sparse_max_n, " or fewer participants."
          )
        },
        "-2 = strongly negative; +2 = strongly positive."
      )
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_family = "Lato", base_size = 18) +
    theme(
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 40),
      axis.text.x = x_axis_text,
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 40),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing = grid::unit(1.2, "lines"),
      plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "italic", size = 14)
    )
}

basic topological and confidence interval visualizations because they were relatively intuitive and

distracting, as they increased perceptual clutter and diverted attention from the underlying signal.

made it difficult to distinguish signal magnitude from uncertainty. I believe adjacent plots showing
the signal and its uncertainty separately could be a more effective approach. They allow researchers
to compare both dimensions without overloading a single visualization. My suggestion would be to
evaluate these approaches not only in terms of interpretation accuracy and response time but also
perceived cognitive workload, visual search efficiency, and user preference. It may also be valuable
to investigate whether visualization preferences differ between experienced EEG researchers and
beginners. Overall, the study addresses an important issue in scientific visualization: how to
communicate statistical uncertainty while maintaining perceptual clarity and supporting reliable
interpretation.
